title: Choose TokenWatch's new world
question: The roll assigned The Running Glass. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Every option answers 'am I about to hit a limit?' first.

options.label: The Running Glass
options.lineage: sand timers, ship's glasses and laboratory hourglasses
options.thesis: Every quota window is a sand glass: what's left sits in the bulb, and a reset turns the glass.
materials: blown glass drawn as hairline vessels
options.viewport: A rack of glasses, the emptiest one first and tallest; its sand reads '7% left' in big tabular numerals with the reset countdown engraved under it, healthy providers shrink to short glasses in a row below.
options.risk: Skeuomorph kitsch if the glass gets shine, wood or brass; it must stay a drawn instrument, flat hairlines and real numbers.

raised.raise: Each glass is engraved with graduation ticks, and your alert threshold is a marked line on the glass, so 'about to hit' is a visible line the sand has crossed.
Glasses sit in a fixed rack of equal cells; a stale or failed reading is struck through in the cell instead of hidden.
A failed refresh attaches as an errata slip to its glass, in the one alert color held out of every other use.
One numeral size for every percent; rank comes from weight and order, never from shrinking a number.

options.label: Dark Cockpit
options.lineage: airliner caution and warning panels (the 'dark cockpit' philosophy)
options.thesis: Normal is dark and silent; only a window nearing its limit lights up, amber for caution and red for warning.
options.viewport: A dark annunciator grid with one lens per provider window; healthy ones are unlit legends, the 7%-left Codex weekly lens glows amber with its reset time stenciled beside it.
options.risk: Familiar: amber-on-black instrument panels are where many developer dashboards already land.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.thesis: Giant cropped numerals on flat provider-colored tiles; the type is the interface.
options.viewport: A black panorama where the riskiest window is a full-width tile reading '7% left' at poster size, cropped off the right edge.
options.case: Wins clarity, since the numbers can't be missed; loses audience fit, because Metro reads as a dead platform to an Android user.
options.risk: Fights Material navigation and Back expectations if the panorama is taken literally.

options.label: Departure Board
options.thesis: Each window is a departure row: provider, window, % left and 'back at' time, flapping when it changes.
options.viewport: A ruled board sorted by least left; the Codex weekly row's lamp is amber and its 'back at Sun 08:30' column is the loudest thing on screen.
options.case: Wins clarity for reset times; loses on 'about to hit', which a timetable treats as a delay rather than the headline.
options.risk: Per-character flap animation is costly in Compose and must collapse under 'Remove animations'.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Percent numerals built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.viewport: Monumental grid-built '7%' over a faint blue construction grid.
options.case: Loses both: a poster system, not a glance tool.
options.kept: Graduation ticks and the alert line engraved on each glass.
options.risk: Decorative grid noise on a small screen.

options.label: Event Catalog
options.thesis: Every window a stamp-sized cell, the risky ones circled in pen.
options.viewport: A packed cell grid with three windows circled.
options.case: Loses both: built for hundreds of items, and TokenWatch has six.
options.kept: A fixed rack of equal cells, with stale readings struck through.
options.risk: Density with nothing to fill it.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.lineage: boxed-software reference manuals with tab dividers
options.thesis: Screens as tabbed divider boards with acetate leaves.
options.viewport: A chrome-yellow divider with provider leaves hinged on top.
options.case: Loses both: a reading form for a glance task.
options.kept: Failures as an errata slip in one reserved alert color.
options.risk: Heavy material for a one-second check.

options.label: Timetable Rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank carried by weight, case and reversal.
options.viewport: A raked rack of slides, one per provider.
options.case: Loses both: raked containers hurt scanning and touch.
options.kept: One numeral size; rank by weight and order.
options.risk: Raked layout fights Android touch targets.

canonCard.label: Material You, done properly
canonCard.thesis: A standard Material 3 app at full craft: dynamic color, expressive type, sorted cards.
canonCard.viewport: Large top app bar, the riskiest window promoted to a hero card, others as compact list items.
canonCard.risk: This is what you just called too generic, polished.
